title: arXiv Mathematics — daily notable papers, 21 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This is an inferred notable-paper ranking, not a measured popularity ranking; citation and independent-attention evidence is limited for the newly announced papers.

sections.title: A Solution to the Kohayakawa-Prömel-Rödl Conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove that for all finite graphs G and H with |V(G)|=k≥2 and |V(H)|=t≥2, their induced Ramsey number satisfies r_ind(G,H)≤t^(60k²+3), resolving the 1998 Kohayakawa–Prömel–Rödl conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove r_ind(G,H)≤t^(60k²+3) for all k,t≥2; the introduction states the sharper intermediate bound 7t^(60k²)≤t^(60k²+3).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite undirected simple graphs; k=|V(G)|≥2 and t=|V(H)|≥2. The bound is an upper bound on the minimum order of a two-edge-coloured host forcing a red induced G or blue induced H.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated exponent is large; the abstract gives no matching lower bound or claim of optimality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a resolution of a named 1998 conjecture with a uniform explicit polynomial bound for every eligible graph pair; this is a concrete, broad-scope result rather than a recency-only pick.

sections.title: One-Ring Bourgain Alternative And A 5-Decimal Bound On The Dimension Of Harmonic Measure
sections.abstract: The authors improve upper bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of harmonic measure—to at most 3−10⁻⁵ in R³ and 4−10⁻⁷ in R⁴—and for every n≥3 give the additional bound n−(n−1)^−(2n+6.12√n), using a new thin-ring estimate and cubes in general position.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the stated 3D and 4D bounds and, for n≥3, the additional estimate n−(n−1)^−(2n+6.12√n); their one-ring alternative shows that a sufficiently thin surrounding ring with no large holes makes Brownian entry into the enclosed cube unlikely.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Harmonic measure on domains in Euclidean Rⁿ, for n≥3. In R³ and R⁴ the claimed bounds are respectively 3−10⁻⁵ and 4−10⁻⁷.
sections.unique_caveat: The bounds remain very close to the ambient dimension and do not reach Bishop's conjectured sharp bound; the authors list ten challenges toward it.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract quantifies improvements over prior bounds in dimensions three and four, cross-lists analysis, PDE, and probability, and identifies a new geometric estimate; these are checkable mathematical-significance signals.

sections.title: Balanced subgraph counts and quasirandomness: a proof of the Janson–Sós conjecture
sections.abstract: For every fixed finite simple graph F with at least two edges, the authors prove that the random-graph asymptotics of symmetrized F-copy counts across all balanced vertex partitions characterize p-quasirandom graph sequences, including when F has isolated vertices.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the conjectured quasirandomness characterization for all fixed finite simple F with at least two edges. The introduction states that the equivalent unsymmetrized formulation also follows.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A graph sequence with vertex count tending to infinity, fixed F, and p∈(0,1]; the asymptotic symmetrized subgraph-count condition is uniform over balanced partitions into |V(F)| classes.
sections.unique_caveat: The characterization is conditional on the specified balanced-partition count data; the result does not say that one observed count or an unbalanced partition suffices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is an explicit proof of the Janson–Sós conjecture, extending the result to every eligible F, including graphs with isolated vertices; the arXiv introduction identifies the conjecture and its prior scope.

sections.title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
sections.abstract: The authors combine o-minimal point-counting with an Ax–Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions and exponentials to prove sparsity for algebraic varieties containing tuples of Bessel zeros, with an application to spectral sets of the unit ball and Fuglede's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed κ≥0 other than 1/2, the authors bound the number of maximal Bessel-special subvarieties of height at most H in a given algebraic variety by C(V,κ,ε)H^ε; for positive half-integer κ other than 1/2 they give a polylogarithmic bound. They also state an Ax–Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions and exponentials.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bessel functions of fixed parameter; the sparsity theorem concerns algebraic V⊂(C×)ⁿ and maximal special subvarieties up to height H≥1. The improved polylogarithmic estimate has the stated positive half-integer restriction.
sections.unique_caveat: The main sparsity statement excludes κ=1/2, and the authors say their constants are not effective; they explain that the excluded parameter has zeros πZ and their approach breaks down there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper connects classical analysis and mathematical logic, supplies a functional-transcendence result and a point-counting application, and the introduction states a quantitative sparsity theorem rather than only a proposed framework.

sections.title: Space-time localized nonuniqueness for the inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations
sections.abstract: For the three-dimensional torus, the author constructs weak solutions of the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier–Stokes equations that match a smooth solution outside a prescribed space-time cylinder yet differ inside it, under specified density and velocity regularity conditions.
sections.claimed_result: The author constructs such weak solutions for every 0<s<3/2 and p>1 sufficiently close to 1, with strictly positive density in C_t L^p and velocity in C_t H^s, using concentrated transported density profiles and localized inverse-divergence operators.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Inhomogeneous incompressible Navier–Stokes on the 3D torus; prescribed smooth fields must satisfy necessary mass and spatial first-moment conditions. The solutions agree with a given smooth solution outside a compact subset of a chosen cylinder.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is limited to the stated low-density-integrability and velocity-regularity regime, and the construction includes non-renormalized density; it is not a claim of nonuniqueness for every conventional solution class.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims space-time localized nonuniqueness, including infinitely many solutions equal to rest outside a cylinder, and gives a concrete convex-integration construction; this is a distinct, sharply specified result in a central PDE.

sections.title: Local well-posedness of wave kinetic equations associated with water waves
sections.abstract: The authors establish local well-posedness for pure-gravity waves with two-dimensional interfaces in weighted Sobolev spaces and for one-dimensional gravity-capillary interfaces in weighted L∞ spaces, while identifying immediate regularity loss and failure of continuity in the latter setting.
sections.claimed_result: For pure-gravity waves with 2D interfaces, the authors prove propagation of weighted-Sobolev regularity and continuous dependence in the same topology. For gravity-capillary waves with 1D interfaces, they prove existence, uniqueness, and continuity in a weaker topology in weighted L∞, and show that added regularity is generally lost instantly.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Wave kinetic equations associated with the two specified water-wave regimes: pure gravity/2D interfaces and gravity-capillary/1D interfaces.
sections.unique_caveat: In the gravity-capillary case, continuity in time and continuous dependence in the weighted L∞ norm fail even for smooth compactly supported data; this is part of the authors' instability result, not ordinary well-posedness in that norm.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives two contrasting well-posedness theories and identifies degenerate three-wave resonances as the mechanism behind the capillary instability; its math.AP/math-ph cross-list reflects the analysis–physics interface.
